name: New Gas-Based Urea Plants: NIPU-2026 Capacity Wave
scope: NIPU-2026 (approved 15 Jul 2026) and the listed Indian companies that sponsor, supply gas to, or build the planned 8-9 new gas-based 1.27 Mtpa urea plants.

summary.one_line: NIPU-2026 restarts urea capex with a tighter 12-16% RoE band. So far only two of the 8-9 planned plants have a public sponsor: Chambal's ~Rs 10,000 cr fourth Gadepan plant, still awaiting board approval, and the GAIL-RCF Vidarbha MoU, with no cost or equity split disclosed. EPC and equipment awards have not yet been made public.
key_points: The Cabinet approved NIPU-2026 on 15 Jul 2026. It separates fixed and variable costs, sets an RoE band of 12% minimum to 16% maximum, and converts fixed costs into INR after four years. The government says it will save more than Rs 250 cr per plant compared with NIP-2012 (S1, S2).

The policy targets about 10 Mt of new capacity from 8-9 gas-based plants of about 1.27 Mtpa each. Plants commissioned within five years of notification get incentives for the following eight years (S3).

The import gap widened sharply. FY26 urea imports were 103.50 lakh t, up 83% from 56.47 lakh t in FY25, while domestic output fell to 293.26 lakh t from 306.67 lakh t (S5). ICRA puts imports at about 27% of FY26 requirement (S4).

ICRA expects fertiliser companies to commit Rs 80,000-90,000 cr of capex over the six months from Aug 2026, with commissioning in about 3.5-4 years. It estimates EBITDA for a standard 1.27 Mtpa unit at Rs 250-280 cr lower than under NIP-2012, where the RoE band was 12-20% (S4).

Chambal is preparing a fourth Gadepan urea plant at about Rs 10,000 cr. It has received technical bids, expected financial bids by mid-October 2026, and the project still needs board and government approval. Commissioning is targeted for 2030-31 (S7, S8, S10).

GAIL and RCF signed an MoU on 29 Jul 2026 for a 1.27 MMTPA gas-based urea plant in Vidarbha, Maharashtra, along GAIL's Mumbai-Nagpur-Jharsuguda pipeline, to be built through an SPV. Equity split and cost have not been disclosed (S6).

Chambal's nearer-term earnings are driven by Gadepan-III losing its NIP-2012 benefits from December 2026. Elara assumes about a one-third cut in G-III EBITDA per tonne and calls FY27E the likely peak year for PAT (S9).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Chambal: the brownfield site, land, in-principle gas approval and advanced pre-project engineering could let it commission first among NIPU sponsors, which Elara calls its unique selling point (S7, S9).
GAIL: it gains a co-owned anchor gas customer on its MNJPL pipeline (S6). Each 1.27 Mtpa plant needs about 2.2 mmscmd of gas (S4).

EPC and equipment makers: this is pipeline, not orders. ICRA expects Rs 80,000-90,000 cr of commitments (S4). L&T Heavy Engineering makes urea reactors and strippers (S16), and EIL has recent fertiliser PMC wins abroad (S15). No NIPU-specific award has been disclosed yet.

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Returns are diluted: the RoE ceiling falls from 20% to 16% (S4), and Chambal's management has said the new plant's returns are dilutive compared with NIP-2012 (S11).
Gas costs and supply: imported LNG supplied about 85% of fertiliser-sector gas in FY26, against 64% in FY21, and the pool gas price was about USD 19/mmBtu in April 2026 (S4).
Subsidy dependence: FY27 fertiliser subsidy is budgeted at Rs 1.71 tn, against Rs 1.86 tn RE in FY26 (S7). Chambal had Rs 24.62 bn of subsidy outstanding at the end of Q1FY27 (S7).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Chambal's evaluation of financial bids and its board's final investment decision; financial bids were expected by mid-October 2026 (S8, S10).
Incorporation of the GAIL-RCF SPV, its equity split and project cost (S6).
Government decision on Gadepan-III returns after December 2026 (S7, S9).
The DoF names remaining sponsors among its 'several proposals' (S2), and the first EPC/LSTK awards.

subsections.title: What NIPU-2026 is and how it differs from NIP-2012

blocks.text: The CCEA approved the National Investment Policy for Urea-2026 on 15 Jul 2026 to encourage fresh investment in gas-based urea units. Its predecessor, NIP-2012, closed its investment window in October 2019 (S1, S2). NIP-2012 produced six new plants: four JVs with nominated PSUs and two private projects (S2).

blocks.caption: NIPU-2026 vs NIP-2012: key terms
rows: Fixed cost converted to INR after 4 years at prevailing rate
Plants commissioned within 5 years of notification get incentives for the following 8 years
EBITDA lower by Rs 250-280 cr; greenfield cumulative DSCR 1.26x over 8 years

blocks.text: None of the sources we opened give the gas-pooling mechanics or the formal DoF implementation guidelines for NIPU-2026. ICRA says the floor and ceiling realisations have also been reduced but does not give figures (S4). This report does not fill those gaps.

According to PIB, India has 33 operating urea units with 269.42 LMT of reassessed or installed capacity (S1). ICRA puts domestic capacity at 30.6 MMTPA and demand at about 39.9 Mt (S4); the two capacity figures use different bases. FY26 imports nearly doubled as domestic production fell (S5). EY India estimates that each Mt of domestic capacity replacing imports saves USD 300-500 mn a year in foreign exchange (S3).

blocks.title: India urea: domestic production vs imports
blocks.source: Source: Govt data in Parliament via India Seatrade News (S5)

blocks.text: The DoF says it has received 'several proposals' from public and private companies (S2) but has not published a list. We found two NIPU-linked projects with public, listed sponsors. Namrup-IV in Assam (12.7 LMT, Rs 10,601.4 cr) was approved separately in March 2025 and is not confirmed as a NIPU-2026 project (S12).

blocks.caption: Identified new urea projects (as of 2 Nov 2026)
rows: Technical bids received; financial bids expected mid-Oct 2026; board and GoI approval pending; commissioning 2030-31
MoU signed 29 Jul 2026; equity split not disclosed
AVFCCL: Assam Govt 40%, NFL 18%, Oil India 18%, HURL 13%, BVFCL 11%

blocks.text: We found no exchange filing or credible report of a NIPU-2026 urea proposal from Coromandel, GSFC, Deepak, Zuari, Paradeep or Madras Fertilizers. A capital-markets brief described RCF and NFL as candidates, but we could not confirm it from primary sources, so it is not relied on here.

subsections.title: Size of the capex cycle and the EPC opportunity

blocks.text: ICRA expects Rs 80,000-90,000 cr of capex commitments over about six months from August 2026. It says capex control and utilisation above 95% will be critical to returns (S4). At about Rs 10,000 cr per plant (S7, S12), 8-9 plants would be broadly consistent with ICRA's figure.

items: Chambal is tendering on an LSTK/EPC basis (S10). No contractor has been named publicly.
Engineers India won a Rs 618 cr PMC/EPCM order for an African fertiliser plant in September 2025 (S15). We found no NIPU-2026 order for it.
L&T Heavy Engineering makes urea reactors, carbamate condensers, urea strippers and high-pressure exchangers (S16), the critical long-lead items for any new plant.

Micro-cap Konstelec Engineers won a PDIL award (25 Jun 2026) for construction power and cable re-routing at the AVFCCL Namrup ammonia-urea plant (S14). It is an example of electrical-contracting work, but on the pre-NIPU Namrup project.

subsections.title: Chambal Fertilisers: fourth plant and the Gadepan-III benefit cliff

blocks.text: Chambal has three urea plants at Gadepan with about 3.3 MTPA of total capacity (S7). For the fourth plant it has acquired additional land, received in-principle gas supplier approval and advanced its pre-project engineering. SKP reports a tentative commissioning date of FY30 (S7); Investing.com reports 2030 or 2031 (S10). A third-party summary of the Q1FY27 call says management will keep its dividend payout at about 25% even with the capex, and has acknowledged that returns are dilutive compared with NIP-2012 (S11). Net borrowing was about Rs 2 bn at the end of Q1FY27 (S7). Management's FY26 commentary was that funding is not a significant challenge (S11).

Sources differ on when the Gadepan-III benefits end. SKP says 'Q4FY27E' in one place and 'December 2026' in another (S7). Elara and Arihant say December 2026 (S8, S9). Elara builds in about a one-third cut in G-III EBITDA per tonne from December 2026, and expects PAT to fall in FY28E before recovering only by about FY30 (S9). The new plant would only start contributing after that trough.

blocks.caption: Broker estimates for Chambal (Rs mn): wide dispersion on FY28E

blocks.text: Under the MoU, GAIL contributes its gas value chain and infrastructure, and RCF contributes fertiliser manufacturing, operations, project execution and marketing. The site lies along GAIL's MNJPL pipeline (S6). The equity split, project cost and SPV name have not been disclosed (S6), so neither company's capex or earnings impact can be quantified yet. If the cost is similar to the other ~1.27 Mtpa projects (about Rs 10,000 cr, S7, S12) and debt:equity is 70:30 as at Namrup (S12), equity needs would be about Rs 3,000 cr shared between the partners. This is our illustrative arithmetic, not a disclosed figure.

We found no evidence of a NIPU-driven re-rating. Chambal traded around Rs 439-441 after the policy (S7, S9), lower over 12 months, as the market weighed the end of Gadepan-III benefits against the new plant. At least three brokers (Elara, Arihant, SKP) discussed NIPU in their Q1FY27 notes on Chambal (S7, S8, S9). We found little broker coverage of NIPU for RCF or GAIL.

items: ICRA (Girishkumar Kadam): the urea capex cycle should take off and debt coverage should stay comfortable, but upside is lower than under NIP-2012. Dependence on imported gas is the key risk (S4).
Elara: early preparatory work could let Chambal start operations earliest. Long-term returns will be 'subdued' because the G-III incentive is withdrawn; FY27E may be peak PAT (S9).
Arihant: the fourth plant is 'the key catalyst', with about Rs 100,000 mn capex and 2030 commissioning, but its ROE is dilutive compared with NIP-2012 (S8).
SKP: once optimised, the project would make Chambal the largest single-location urea producer in India, and common manpower and infrastructure would improve EBITDA per tonne (S7).
EY India (Satyam Shivam Sundaram): each Mt of capacity that replaces imports saves USD 300-500 mn of foreign exchange a year (S3).

Gas availability and price: LNG made up about 85% of fertiliser-sector gas in FY26, and the pool gas price was about USD 19/mmBtu in April 2026, up from about USD 13 earlier (S4). Chambal's gas price was USD 17.25/MMBtu in Q1FY27 (S7).
Returns dilution: the RoE ceiling is 16%, against 20% before (S4), and fixed costs convert to INR after four years (S1).
Subsidy and working capital: FY27 subsidy BE is Rs 1.71 tn (S7). Payment delays raise working-capital costs (S7).
Long gestation: ICRA expects 3.5-4 years to commissioning, with self-sufficiency improving materially only from 2030-31 (S4). Namrup-IV has a 48-month schedule (S12).
PSU execution: the GAIL-RCF project is still at MoU stage, with no cost, timeline or equity split disclosed (S6).

companies.name: Chambal Fertilisers and Chemicals
companies.role: Largest private-sector urea maker, with three Gadepan plants of about 3.3 MTPA (S7). It is preparing a fourth plant of about Rs 10,000 cr under NIPU-2026 (S7, S10).
companies.impact: Most direct listed play, but near-term earnings face the end of Gadepan-III benefits from December 2026. Returns on the new plant are dilutive compared with NIP-2012, and FID is still pending (S9, S11).

companies.name: Rashtriya Chemicals and Fertilizers
companies.role: PSU urea maker, partnering GAIL in a 1.27 MMTPA Vidarbha SPV and bringing manufacturing, execution and marketing (S6).
companies.impact: Volume-growth option from about 2030. Its equity share and capex are undisclosed, so the earnings impact cannot be quantified yet (S6).

companies.name: GAIL (India)
companies.role: Gas transmission and marketing. Co-sponsor of the Vidarbha SPV, with the plant sited on its MNJPL pipeline (S6).
companies.impact: Each plant needs about 2.2 mmscmd of gas (S4), which would add anchor pipeline load. The equity commitment is undisclosed (S6).

companies.name: National Fertilizers
companies.role: PSU urea maker with an 18% stake (about Rs 572.45 cr) in the AVFCCL Namrup-IV JV (S13).
companies.impact: Exposure is to the pre-NIPU Namrup capacity addition. We found no confirmed NIPU-2026 proposal (S12, S13).

companies.name: Oil India
companies.role: Holds 18% of the Namrup-IV urea JV in Assam (S12).
companies.impact: Minor equity outlay in a 12.7 LMT plant. The plant is a potential gas offtaker in the Northeast (S12).

companies.name: Engineers India
companies.role: PMC and EPCM consultant with fertiliser credentials, including a Rs 618 cr order for an African fertiliser plant (S15).
companies.impact: Credible bidder for NIPU PMC work, but we found no NIPU-2026 order yet (S15, S4).

companies.name: Larsen & Toubro
companies.role: Its Heavy Engineering arm makes urea reactors, strippers, carbamate condensers and high-pressure exchangers (S16).
companies.impact: Supplier of long-lead equipment for any new plant. Orders depend on sponsor FIDs; none disclosed (S16, S4).

companies.name: Petronet LNG
companies.role: LNG importer that has signed a Rs 1,200 cr regasification deal with a Deepak Fertilisers subsidiary at Dahej (S19).
companies.impact: New urea plants raise LNG demand: LNG supplied about 85% of fertiliser-sector gas in FY26 (S4). It is not a partner in any announced NIPU plant.

companies.name: Konstelec Engineers
companies.role: Micro-cap electrical EPC contractor; won a PDIL award for work at the AVFCCL Namrup ammonia-urea plant (S14).
companies.impact: Small-cap illustration of contracting opportunities around new urea plants. The award relates to Namrup, not NIPU-2026 (S14).

method: First edition, researched on 1-2 Nov 2026 using web searches and fetches. Policy terms come from the PIB release and news reports of it. Sector economics come from ICRA's August 2026 thematic, as reported by KNN. Company detail comes from broker notes (SKP, Arihant, Elara) read in full from the PDFs, plus news coverage of the GAIL-RCF MoU. We searched for NIPU proposals by other listed fertiliser makers and for EPC/equipment orders across large, mid and small caps; the only small-cap link found was Namrup-related, not NIPU. Management call commentary (S11) comes from a third-party summary and should be checked against the transcript. For undated web pages (S16, S19) the access date is used. One fertiliser news site contained embedded instructions aimed at AI tools; we ignored it and did not cite it. numbers.json was not present in the folder, so no screener figures were used.

plant_sponsors: Listed companies that have publicly announced or are evaluating a new NIPU-2026 urea plant
